candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 35:1 (Death of Rebekah (35:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And in the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee... Rebecca called Jacob her son... and said unto him: My son, do honour thy brother, thy father Isaac, all the days of thy life, until the day of his death' — Rebekah's parting instruction to Jacob to honour Isaac. Tewahedo filial-piety tradition preserves Rebekah's blessing structure as canonical pattern: the mother's instruction binding the son to the father's honour.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 35:6 (Death of Rebekah (35:6)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Esau is to thee from time eternal a foe, but I trust that thou wilt confess thy ways to him and that he will yet repent of his evil purpose, and that mercy will reach him' — Rebekah's deathbed words to Jacob preserve a remarkable canonical hope for Esau's eventual repentance. Tewahedo eschatological hope (the universalism-leaning emphasis that the Tewahedo holds in tension with apokatastasis-rejection — the Tewahedo neither dogmatically affirms nor dogmatically denies universal-final-repentance) finds canonical matriarchal anchor here: even the most-rejected covenant-line brother is canonically hoped-for. The Tewahedo's distinctive pastoral generosity toward non-Tewahedo Christians and even toward those of other faiths in salvation-trust questions draws on Rebekah's witness.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 35:18 (Death of Rebekah (35:18)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And she died, the same day, and her two sons buried her, Esau and Jacob, in the double cave near Sarah her mother-in-law' — Esau and Jacob buried Rebekah TOGETHER in the Machpelah cave, in fraternal cooperation at her funeral despite their lifelong rivalry. Jubilees emphasizes this unique reconciliation-at-the-mother's-grave moment. The Tewahedo pastoral tradition of family-reunion-at-funerals (estranged-family-members reconciling at the matriarch's or patriarch's funeral) draws canonical warrant here: even where the relationship cannot be repaired in life, the death of the parent provides a divinely-arranged occasion for partial reconciliation. The Tewahedo's family-funeral liturgy preserves a moment of joint-prayer-by-estranged-children, anchored typologically in this verse.
